title: Switzerland hosts the Summit on Peace in Ukraine at Bürgenstock
body:
The Summit on Peace in Ukraine took place on 15 and 16 June 2024 at the Bürgenstock resort in the canton of Nidwalden, Switzerland. Switzerland organised the summit at Ukraine's request. Preparations were led by the Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs, with an interdepartmental steering group under Federal Councillor Ignazio Cassis, and the cantons of Nidwalden, Lucerne and Zurich took part in planning.

Switzerland invited more than 160 delegations, and about 100 attended, including 57 heads of state or government. Russia was not invited.

The final communiqué affirmed that the UN Charter and international law, including Ukraine's territorial integrity and sovereignty, form the basis for a peace process. It stated that Ukrainian nuclear power plants, including Zaporizhzhia, should be secured and placed under Ukraine's sovereign control and International Atomic Energy Agency supervision. It called for free and secure commercial shipping, which matters for countries relying on Ukrainian grain exports. It also called for an exchange of all prisoners of war and for the return of deported Ukrainian children and arbitrarily detained civilians. The communiqué said that other countries, including Russia, should be involved in the process, and that states which did not attend could still endorse it.
